background_notes.fact: An integer basis of M which is also a complex basis of the finite-dimensional V can be reindexed by I when |I|=dim_C V=n.

grounds.reason: H004 supplies the simultaneous lattice and complex basis.
N001 supplies finite dimension n and |I|=n.

background_notes.justification: Any basis of an n-dimensional vector space has n elements: the finite exchange argument bounds an independent family by the size of a spanning family, applied in both directions to two bases. A bijection between its index set and I then reindexes both basis properties without changing any vector.

background_notes.fact: For a Z-linear endomorphism T of M, scalar extension to any commutative Z-algebra S is the S-linear endomorphism of S⊗_Z M determined by s⊗m↦s⊗T(m). For S=R and complex-linear T on V restricting to M, this extension intertwines μ with T. An injective R-linear map carrying an R-basis to a complex basis identifies its image as a free R-module of that rank spanning V.

grounds.reason: H004 supplies preservation of M by every divided power.
H002 supplies h=xy−yx, so h also preserves M after x=X_1 and y=Y_1.
V_K=M⊗_Z K; K is a commutative Z-algebra as a field.

background_notes.justification: The displayed pure-tensor formula respects additivity and integer balancing because T is Z-linear; hence it descends to the tensor product. Equality with Tμ holds on pure tensors and therefore on their finite sums. Every kernel vector has a finite expansion in the tensor basis; its images give a complex-linear relation, so all R-coefficients vanish since R embeds in C. The images of the basis then freely generate the image and span V over C. The same tensor construction with M⊗_Z K gives the asserted K-linear induced operators.

background_notes.fact: If p is prime and 0≤j≤λ<p, then p does not divide binom(λ,j), and binom(λ,j) is a unit of R=Z_(p).

grounds.reason: A rational with denominator prime to p lies in R.

background_notes.justification: Every positive factor in λ! lies strictly between 0 and p. Reduction modulo p is in the field Z/pZ, so the product of these nonzero residues is nonzero; the empty product for λ=0 is 1. The integer identity λ!=binom(λ,j)j!(λ−j)! then rules out p dividing binom(λ,j). Its rational reciprocal belongs to R and multiplies it to 1.
